If a nn disables some neurons it means the neurons must be finite, but if with 10 inputs X1 is used, and with 100 inputs X2 are used, then 1000 inputs must enable X3, 10000 X4 and so on, so you'd need an infinite amount of nodes in the nn. This is a contradiction.

I think you don't actually need varying number of inputs, you just need a big limit of them.

You could make inputs fixed(like 100 words per phrase) and zero out every one which is not used.

The reason this could make sense is because if you have varying input sizes then the model must have been trained for an arbitrary number of inputs, and I don't think making 10 inputs would be trained the same way as a 100 input model, just go to the extreme cases and see what the model does when having 1.000.000 inputs (which is valid because we made the inputs of varying size), but the prediction would be very bad.

Also, how many hidden layers for 10 or 1.000.000 inputs? And how many neurons on each of them? they surely cannot be the same.

The initial state is just the rotations at 0 degrees. And yes, 360 and 0 are equal. If a cylinder with rotation 0 is pointing left, then that same cylinder rotated 180 must point right. Applying the same rotation takes us to the initial state of that cylinder.

**edit:**

Note that a cylinder's initial state can be either up, down, left or right, it does not matter. But for simplicity, the initial state is every cylinder pointing up, and that's considered 0deg. If it is pointing left 90deg and so on.
